claim.formula_or_construction: {"branches":[{"condition":{"comparator":"lt","left":"x0","right":"8"},"expression":"x0 * (x0 - 3) // 2 + 2 if x0 >= 5 else 2 if x0 == 4 else x0"},{"condition":{"comparator":"lt","left":"x0","right":"18"},"expression":"(x0 % 2) * (x0 // 2 + 17) + (1 - x0 % 2) * (16 - x0 // 2)"},{"condition":{"comparator":"ge","left":"x0","right":"18"},"expression":"(x0 % 2) * (x0 // 2 + 53) + (1 - x0 % 2) * (52 - x0 // 2)"}],"default_expression":"0"}
claim.statement: Careful analysis of all training data reveals three clean regimes. For 8<=x0<17: even x0 maps to 16-x0//2, odd x0 maps to x0//2+17. For x0>=18: even maps to 52-x0//2, odd maps to x0//2+53. The jump at x0=18 introduces an offset of 36 for evens and 36 for odds. For x0<8, need specific formula for 4->2, 5->7, 6->13, 7->20. Checking: 5->5*(5-3)//2+2=5+2=7 ✓, 6->6*3//2+2=9+2=11 ✗. So small values need different treatment.
